sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Reverse Logistics and Returned Goods Quality Grading

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil law (Napoleonic system with Luxembourg-specific commercial and company law modifications)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-Hong Kong Double Taxation Agreement (2009, effective 2014)
Luxembourg-Germany Double Taxation Agreement (OECD-compliant current text)
Luxembourg-United States Tax Convention, as amended (to the extent applicable)
EU-UK Trade and Cooperation Agreement (for cross-border logistics and services)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004 on money laundering and terrorist financing, as substantially amended and supplemented by the Law of 18 December 2015 and subsequent implementing acts; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners; Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended; CSSF AML/CFT Regulation 12-02 (consolidated version); Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2020 on the RBE register.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (register accessible only to competent authorities, AML-obliged professionals, and persons demonstrably holding a legitimate interest, not through a fully open public portal)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of a valid passport for each beneficial owner and legal representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consular office or national police authority in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference / due diligence letter from the opening bank of the corporate shareholder (if any)
Certificate of good standing / extract of company register for all corporate shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent commercial registry of the corporate shareholder's jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized power of attorney for the Luxembourg notary and incorporation agent
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the principal's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Personal UBO declaration under Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each ultimate beneficial owner(s), countersigned by a home-country notary

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, managers and authorized signatories against: PEP ranking lists under FATF Recommendation 12 and Luxembourg Law of 12 November 2004; EU consolidated financial sanctions list; UN Security Council resolutions; OFAC SDN list and US non-SDN sectoral sanctions; Luxembourg CSSF high-risk jurisdictions list. A minimum of two independent screening databases must be used; negative news and politically exposed person reviews are completed prior to notarization.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL) – online name and company reservation portal at https://www.lbr.lu
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be capable of being written in Latin script letters; French, German and Luxembourgish are routinely accepted; foreign names require exact Latin transliteration. The name must not conflict with public order provisions of Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915, must contain 'Société à responsabilité limitée' or the abbreviation 'S.à r.l.' as the legal form suffix, and must not be identical or misleadingly similar to any existing registered name in the RCSL index.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The initial RCSL name reservation is valid for 30 days and cannot be extended administratively; the applicant may file a fresh reservation request after expiry. If the name is rejected, a written appeal must be submitted within 15 days to the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg (Commercial Chamber), together with a certified copy of the rejection notice, a statement of grounds, and any amended proposed name. Concurrently, the applicant may submit a revised name to the RCSL registrar without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is permissible solely through a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent that provides a physical address, safety deposit for formal legal documents, and automatic forwarding of all administrative and tax notices. For the declared activity of cross-border reverse logistics, a purely virtual office without any physical operational base in Luxembourg is acceptable only for holding the legal seat and central administration; substantial EU logistics operations would normally trigger VAT and customs presence in the actual warehouse jurisdiction.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (10-15%) for a low-risk, standard reverse logistics business incorporated as a SARL, but physical on-site inspections by Luxembourg tax authorities, customs or police become more likely (35-50%) if the company engages in bonded warehousing, import-export or receives target-target trade sanctions alerts.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Luxembourg notary public notarization of the articles of association and signing of the incorporation deed
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (notarial tariff for a standard SARL incorporation; EU 1,600)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCSL registration filing fee for the new Luxembourg SARL
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff (Luxembourg business registry fee schedule 2025)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) initial filing of beneficial owner information
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff as amended by Grand-Ducal Regulation of 1 February 2020

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Official gazette publication of incorporation extract (Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations – RESA)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Justice / RESA publication service
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff for mandatory public publication

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization handling fee per document (5 documents required)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs (Apostille office) and external courier
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff per Hague Apostille Convention (USD 45 per document)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed domiciliation service for registered office in Luxembourg (12-month initial term)
Bank account opening and AML onboarding support (Luxembourg credit institution or bank-fintech alternative)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark for corporate account onboarding (EUR 500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Pre-incorporation UBO piercing, PEP/sanctions screening, name clearance and legal drafting by Luxembourg counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark (EUR 2,000 fixed fee for Stage 1 advisory)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), Articles 109 to 158 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), R.C.S. Luxembourg.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarial Deed of Incorporation (Acte constitutif) and Coordinated Articles of Association (Statuts coordonnés) permanently filed through the RCS e-filing platform.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Statutory minimum share capital is EUR 12,000. At least 25% (EUR 3,000) must be fully paid up and deposited in a Luxembourg bank in a blocked escrow account prior to notarial signature; the account remains frozen until the RCS registration certificate is issued.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that each subscriber’s subscription to the shares of the Company, as stated in the subscription list annexed to the Minutes, is hereby accepted and the allotment of shares is confirmed. RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company is fixed at the address indicated in the statutes, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and that the Notary and any representative are authorised to file the statutes with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS). RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed as officers of the Company: [Name] as Manager (Gérant) and [Name] as authorised signatory. The Managers are granted full powers to operate the Company’s bank accounts and to execute all documents required for the continuation of the reverse-logistics business, subject to statutory limitations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Bank Account Blockage and Capital Deposit
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg banks licensed by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary blocked escrow account in the name of the future company; deposit the statutory share capital (at least EUR 12,000, with a minimum of 25% paid in); obtain a capital payment certificate (Certificat de blocage) from the bank confirming the deposit and that the account is frozen until registration. The certificate is then delivered to the notary.
required_dossiers: Identity passports of the future shareholders and managers
Bank KYC forms and beneficial ownership declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If additional AML/KYC documentation is required, provide source-of-funds evidence and restate the deposit; a substitute bank may be selected if the first bank delays.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Execution of the Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Notaire) for the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary reviews the statutes, capital deposit certificate, and appointment of managers; the shareholders or their representatives execute the incorporation deed before the notary; the notary signs and transmits the electronic file to the RCS for registration.
required_dossiers: Final coordinated statutes signed by all subscribers
Subscription list and first shareholders' call
Consent of the managers to act
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary requires amendments to the statutes, execute a supplementary notarial deed to correct the wording and re-sign the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RCS Registration and Company Number Activation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the Luxembourg Business Registers e-request platform
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the incorporation file through the LBR e-request; the RCS verifies the file, assigns the corporate registration number, and issues the certificate of registration (Certificat d'immatriculation). The company also obtains its Legal Entity Identifier (LEI).
required_dossiers: Proof of registered office (lease deed or consent of the landlord)
Copy of the bank blocked account certificate
Manager's identity documents and criminal record extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: On any RCS query (e.g., missing document or schedule), the notary resubmits the corrected file through the same e-request within 5 business days; an administrative refusal may be appealed before the competent court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Official Publication in the Recueil des Sociétés et Associations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS Publication Office / Central Legislation Service (Service central de législation), Journal officiel du Grand-Duché de Luxembourg
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the RCS automatically transmits an extract for publication in the Recueil; the company pays the publication fee; publication is required for the incorporation to be opposable to third parties.
required_dossiers: Proof of payment of the publication fee invoice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed, contact the RCS to confirm payment and request acceleration; verify the correctness of the published extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED) – VAT Office; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) – Corporate Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the tax registration on MyGuichet; the company receives its national business number and is automatically registered for corporate income tax (IRC). Apply for a VAT identification number using the standard VAT registration form; file the opening balance sheet within 30 days.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax registration is queried, present the full completed forms and the RCS certificate to the AED/ACD; re-submit a corrected application if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Permit Application for Reverse Logistics Operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for SMEs (Ministère de l'Économie, Direction générale des PME) via MyGuichet
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File an application for a business permit (autorisation d'établissement) for the activity 'other supporting transport activities – ISIC 5229' in the reverse logistics field. The Company's manager must prove professional qualification (at least 3 years relevant professional experience or equivalent training); the manager's criminal record and the lease for the operational site are submitted.
required_dossiers: Copy of the manager's ID and criminal record (casier judiciaire)
Proof of professional competence (diploma or employment certificates)
Copy of the lease agreement or title to the warehouse
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the permit is refused, an administrative appeal may be filed with the Ministry of the Economy within 30 days; an amended application with supplementary proof of qualification can also be submitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Customs EORI Registration for Cross-Border Returned Goods
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Customs and Excise Administration (Administration des douanes et accises) – EORI Unit, via MyGuichet / Union Customs Code system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the EORI (Economic Operators Registration and Identification) registration application online; the company receives its EORI number (LUXXXXXXXX) enabling it to file customs declarations for cross-border returned goods and operate in the EU customs territory. This registration is mandatory if the company performs customs formalities for its reverse logistics business.
required_dossiers: Business permit (or copy of the application receipt)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the EORI application is rejected or queried, correct the file on the customs portal, verify the VAT number with the AED, and resubmit within 2 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy – General Directorate for SMEs (Ministère de l'Économie, Direction générale des PME)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement pour activités logistiques (Business Permit for Logistics Activities) issued under the Law of 2 September 2011

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement – Environmental Agency (Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt from a formal EIA (Category 'D' under the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment); a registered warehouse for reverse logistics does not constitute a Class A–C project. However, any installation for the treatment of e-waste, WEEE, or hazardous mixed returns could trigger a Class 3B EIA screening.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: only sanitary sewage to municipal network (no process water); VOC/air emissions below classification thresholds (no solvent use); noise below 65 dB(A) at the industrial boundary; waste management and transport of returned goods must comply with the Luxembourg Waste Act (Law of 21 March 2012), the EU Waste Shipment Regulation (EC) No 1013/2006, and packaging waste must be sorted by approved waste management operators.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification from the Fire and Rescue Administration (Administration des services de secours – CSS) via the communal authority; structural load inspection of shelving and flooring by an approved control office; occupational clearance from the Labour Inspectorate (Inspection du Travail et des Mines – ITM) covering work safety, first-aid equipment, and compliance with the Grand-Ducal Regulation on workplace safety.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Grand Duchy of Luxembourg — Indirect/VAT: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), VAT returns filed via MyGuichet.lu (e-TVA channel); Direct taxes: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Customs/export formalities: Administration des douanes et accises (Customs & Excise). Central business registry: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR / RCS) accessible through MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: SOP for non-resident owners forming a Luxembourg SARL engaged in ISIC 5229 reverse logistics: (1) reserve corporate name, execute notarial deed of incorporation, and deposit minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 with a Luxembourg credit institution; (2) file incorporation at the RCS/LBR, obtaining the national registration number (matricule); (3) submit the VAT registration application to the AEDT via MyGuichet.lu (form 604 or equivalent electronic declaration); AEDT issues the Luxembourg VAT number with prefix LU + 8 digits; (4) obtain an EORI number from the Administration des douanes et accises before lodging any customs/export declarations; (5) if the SARL is represented by a non-EU principal, appoint an approved Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative who is jointly and severally liable for VAT; (6) complete the beneficial owner declaration in the RBE register. Registration becomes effective from the first taxable transaction with no post-incorporation grace period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation — a resident SARL is a separate taxable person subject to Luxembourg corporate income tax (15% headline CIT plus 7% solidarity surcharge, plus municipal business tax, aggregate approximately 24.94% in Luxembourg City), net wealth tax (0.5% with minimum CIT-based floor), and VAT as a taxable person. Luxembourg does not provide a US-style check-the-box pass-through election for SARLs; no territorial exemption and no tax-exempt zone regime applies — the residence-based system is mitigated by the participation exemption (100% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains) and treaty reliefs.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Available statutory elections: (a) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) under Article 61 of the Luxembourg VAT Law, enabling the SARL and affiliated companies to be treated as one taxable person upon AEDT approval; (b) option to apply VAT to the let of immovable property under Article 44 of the VAT Law; (c) direct-tax fiscal unity (intégration fiscale) regime, election/application available for qualifying 95%-owned resident or Luxembourg permanent establishments of EEA-resident entities, subject to ACD prior approval for the relevant tax year; (d) optional claim of the VAT small-business exemption where annual turnover does not exceed the statutory threshold. Hybrid mismatch outcomes are mandatory under ATAD II transposition and are not elective; advance tax agreements/rulings with the ACD are accessible to confirm treatment of cross-border reverse-logistics fee arrangements.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA — Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) under the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979, as amended, aligned with EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR — Luxembourg: no VAT registration turnover threshold for foreign/non-established suppliers (registration due from the first euro of taxable activity, with mandatory Luxembourg fiscal representative for non-EU principals); established small enterprises may benefit from the Article 57 VAT Law exemption while annual taxable turnover does not exceed EUR 30,000, provided the status is explicitly claimed and the business is not precluded by the legal form or election.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction control (CTC), or digital stamping for B2B invoices. Mandatory e-invoicing applies only to B2G transactions via the PEPPOL network and the national public procurement platform; B2B invoices must satisfy Article 5/6 VAT Law content requirements (sequential numbering, issuer VAT number, delivery details, invoice date and issuance deadline). VAT returns are submitted electronically (e-TVA), VIES validation is required for intra-EU customer VAT numbers, and export declarations must be lodged through the EU customs systems (ECS/Export, NCTS) with the Administration des douanes et accises; no revision of invoice flow or separate fiscal receipt stamping is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating at 0% is available for: (a) goods exported by the SARL to customers established outside the EU, provided the goods physically depart the customs territory of the European Union and an accepted customs export declaration exists; (b) intra-EU dispatches to VAT-registered customers in another Member State where the customer's Luxembourg-independent VAT number is validated via VIES and movement evidence is held; (c) B2B supplies of reverse-logistics, returned-goods grading, and handling services to non-EU customers where the place of supply is outside Luxembourg under the general B2B place-of-supply rule, so that the service is deemed outside the scope of Luxembourg VAT with full input VAT deduction; (d) processing or repair services on goods temporarily imported and re-exported. The SARL must evidence the actual export/exit, the recipient's non-EU business status, and commercial substance of the transaction.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (export declaration lodged via the Administration des douanes et accises / ECS system, with Movement Reference Number and accepted export status)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical departure of returned merchandise from the customs territory of the European Union
Inward Remittance Certificate (or bank SWIFT payment confirmation) evidencing receipt of consideration for the reverse-logistics transaction
Commercial invoice and packing list cross-referencing the export declaration number, EORI number, and Luxembourg VAT number of the SARL
Validated proof of delivery, customs exit records, or customs stamp where available from the exporting office
Contracts, returns-merchandise authorisation records, quality-grading reports, and disposal/reforwarding documentation evidencing commercial substance
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg VAT legislation does not impose a statutory foreign-exchange repatriation deadline for export zero-rating; the 180-day benchmark is the internal treasury control milestone of this dossier. The AEDT may audit the zero-rating file and require the full documentary bundle referenced above. If the export evidence is missing, incomplete, or fraudulent, the 0% rate is denied and Luxembourg VAT at 17% is reassessed from the time of supply, together with late-payment interest (statutory rate under the Collection Law) and administrative penalties up to double the tax due in cases of concealment. Customs law further exposes the SARL to post-clearance recovery of import/export duties and penalties for false declarations. Fabricated bills of lading, simulated remittances, or circular cargo movements constitute VAT fraud, risking criminal fines and imprisonment, joint and several liability of the fiscal representative, publication of penalties, and retroactive clawback within the general five-year prescription period (extended where fraud or abuse is proven).
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.mandatory_fx_repatriation_deadline_note: No statutory Luxembourg FX repatriation deadline for VAT zero-rating; 180 days used as group internal control benchmark.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) within the Eurosystem and the European Central Bank (ECB); the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) is the competent credit-institution and AML/CFT supervisor; the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF/Luxembourg FIU) receives suspicious-transaction reports.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg has no exchange controls. Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union guarantees free movement of capital to and from third countries. The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Profit remittance, dividend distribution, and shareholder-loan repayment to non-residents are unrestricted subject to the standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (15% domestic; 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive with a 12-month holding period) and to statutory BCL/CSSF statistical reporting. No prior authorisation, no FDI screening, and no capital-export restrictions apply to a reverse-logistics SARL (ISIC 5229 / NAICS 488510).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender or mandatory conversion rules exist in Luxembourg. Export receipts in foreign currency may be retained or converted at market rates without any time limit. The only compliance duties are (i) flow-by-flow balance-of-payments reporting to the BCL for all cross-border payment transactions, effected via the reporting bank, and (ii) cash-declaration and AML obligations under the amended Law of 12 November 2004 if physical cash or unusual settlement methods are used.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE / Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: MEDIUM-HIGH for disbursement-only use cases and LOW for primary treasury concentration. A Luxembourg SARL may lawfully use Airwallex or any non-EU/EEA digital EMI only through that EMI's EU/EEA-authorised e-money institution passporting into Luxembourg under the PSD2 and the Law of 10 August 2018 on payment services and e-money (transposing Directive 2009/110/EC). Passport notification to the CSSF by the home-state supervisor is mandatory; the EMI must not breach the Luxembourg banking monopoly (Article 28-1 of the Law of 5 August 1993). Funds safeguarded with an external EMI are not covered by the Luxembourg deposit-guarantee scheme (Fonds de protection des dépôts Luxembourg) and therefore should never replace a tier-1 bank treasury account. Recommended structure: retain BCEE or BNP Paribas as the primary liquidity concentration bank and use Airwallex as a downstream, small-ticket refund rail with capped balances for e-commerce return merchandise.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the established market norm and practically mandatory for a newly incorporated cross-border SARL. Under CSSF Circular 12/552 and the amended Law of 12 November 2004, Luxembourg credit institutions must identify and verify the identity of clients and beneficial owners; CSSF guidance presumes face-to-face verification for non-resident UBOs unless electronic identification offers equivalent assurance. Tier-1 banks (BCEE, BNP Paribas, Société Générale) generally require at least one physical KYC interview of a senior director or UBO, or a notarised and apostilled power of attorney in favour of a locally present manager. Remote video onboarding is only accepted for low-risk EU-resident UBOs and is not reliable in this cross-border logistics blueprint; the safest procedure is one physical visit to Luxembourg during incorporation for signatory verification and UBO interview.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Multi-tier non-resident ownership with opaque ultimate beneficial ownership or UBOs domiciled in jurisdictions with less-developed transparency frameworks.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Luxembourg UBO register extract (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs), RCSL extract (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), notarised articles of association, certified passport copies and proof of residential address of all directors and UBOs, a written control-chain narrative, bank references, and, if any tier exceeds three entities, a legal opinion confirming the effective control chain and absence of undisclosed nominees.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual payment pattern: high-frequency, low-average-ticket cross-border refunds and return-reimbursement wires without clear linkage to original orders or commercial documents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Master service agreements and commercial contracts with e-commerce marketplaces, six months of settlement reports and return-volume forecasts, refund policy, transaction-level audit mapping of each return to an original order ID, sample invoice and credit-note flows, VAT registration certificate (numéro d'identification à la TVA), and a written explanation of the commercial rationale for bulk refund routing.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds opacity for the initial capital injection of EUR 12,000 or for subsequent shareholder loans.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised capital subscription declaration showing 100% payment of the SARL minimum capital, board resolutions approving the capital increase or intercompany loan, three months of bank statements of the contributing shareholder, the UBO's source-of-wealth statement, executed shareholder loan agreements with arm's-length interest terms, and evidence that the injected funds are not commingled with third-party receivables.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or geographic risk arising from returned-goods origin, re-import routes, or counterparties located in non-OECD or partially sanctioned jurisdictions.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: EU consolidated sanctions-list, OFAC and UN screening reports for all counterparties and freight forwarders; customs declarations and country-of-origin certificates; Incoterms contracts with logistics providers; bills of lading / airway bills and return authorisations; a compliance manual embedding evergreen screening under EU Regulation 833/2014; and a documented policy for exception handling of returns transiting embargoed territories.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: SWIFT MT103 (single UETR) from the shareholder's bank to the LU IBAN account of the SARL, with remittance information in field 70 stating the EU balance-of-payments purpose code 'S001' (direct investment – equity capital), the notarial deed reference, and the share-purchase narration. TARGET2 (T2) real-time settlement is used for immediate funds; MT202/MT202 COVER is acceptable for onward cover. The notary's attestation of capital payment and the shareholder bank statement comprise the verification bundle. All cross-border capital flows must be reported flow-by-flow to the BCL by the receiving bank under the Luxembourg balance-of-payments/IOFA statistics regime.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Preferred clearing rails: SEPA Instant Credit Transfer (SCT Inst) and SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EUR-denominated refunds and supplier payments within the Single Euro Payments Area; SWIFT MT103 with UETR for non-EUR supplier disbursements, referencing invoice numbers and customs declarations in field 70. For large return-merchandise settlements above EUR 50,000, a commercial letter of credit under UCP 600 or documentary collections issued by the Luxembourg bank constitute the standard trade-clearing rail. Local ACH (LuxCSD / SEPA settlement) is used for payroll and fiscal payments, and Airwallex is deployed as the fintech refund rail for small-ticket, high-velocity e-commerce reverse-logistics flows. Each disbursement must carry a matching invoice or credit-note reference and HS/CN tariff classification to avoid correspondent-bank de-risking freezes.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD deliverable FX forward contracts under the 1998 ISDA FX Master Agreement, tenors up to 24 months, traded with tier-1 Luxembourg banks
EUR/CNH deliverable FX forward contracts on the offshore-renminbi market to hedge reverse-logistics re-import and China-related cost exposures
Cross-currency swaps (EUR/USD and EUR/CNH) for hedging structural long-term treasury mismatches arising from multi-currency customer flows
Vanilla European-style FX options on EUR/USD and EUR/CNH, collateralised under a CSA, for asymmetric protection without option-premium destabilisation

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible under Luxembourg law but only for non-convertible counterparty currencies (e.g., INR, IDR, certain LatAm pairs); EUR itself, being fully convertible, does not require NDF hedging

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS confirmation of registered company particulars (registered office, managers, directors, statutory purpose and corporate details)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS-LBR)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month following receipt of the LBR annual reminder; reminder is generally aligned with the registration anniversary date.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and injunctions; persistent non-confirmation may trigger judicial strike-off procedures or compulsory dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual statutory financial statements filed with the Luxembourg trade and companies register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés via the eCDF electronic filing portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within seven months after the close of the financial year; for calendar-year SARL, no later than 31 July following the year-end. Shareholder approval must occur within six months of year-end.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines imposed by the RCS registrar; court order obtained by the public prosecutor to compel filing; repeated default can result in strike-off or compulsory winding-up of the SARL.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate tax return covering Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (Luxembourg Inland Revenue)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For calendar-year taxpayers, generally due by 31 December of the year following the tax year; professional tax advisers may receive additional time through the published filing campaign.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default tax assessment, penalty of up to 10% on the additional tax assessed, monthly late-payment interest on unpaid taxes, and possible criminal sanctions for willful non-filing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial owner confirmation filing in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), managed by Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually on or before 31 March following the end of the calendar year, even if no ownership or control changes occurred.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal fines up to EUR 1,250,000 and imprisonment for responsible officers, in addition to administrative fines and possible public notice of non-compliance.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory audit is required for an SARL exceeding at least two of three thresholds in two consecutive financial years: balance sheet total exceeding EUR 4,400,000; net turnover exceeding EUR 8,800,000; average headcount exceeding 50 employees. Small and micro-undertaking exemptions cease for public-interest entities, regulated financial undertakings, or where group audit obligations apply.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the amended Law of 19 December 2002 on the commercial register and annual accounts, together with the Luxembourg chart of accounts; IFRS as endorsed by the EU is permitted for individual statutory accounts and required for consolidated accounts of listed public-interest entities.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Every SARL must complete an annual confirmation of beneficial ownership in the RBE by 31 March of the following year. Any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership occurring during the year must also be declared to the RBE within one month of the transaction. The annual confirmation is mandatory even when no changes have occurred, and share transfers must be properly recorded in the register of members to be effective against third parties.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000 - 20,000 per audit for a typical Luxembourg SARL

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 17% (plus 7% solidarity surcharge and municipal business tax; aggregate rate ~24.94% in Luxembourg City)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Participation exemption (100% exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains under conditions); 80% exemption for qualifying IP income under the Luxembourg IP box regime; investment tax credit for SMEs up to 25% of eligible expenses; notional interest deduction rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 300 (Corporate Income Tax Return), filed via MyGuichet.lu / eCDF (electronic filing mandatory for companies)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: 31 December of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end (extensions generally available to 30 June of the subsequent year upon request)

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company identification: name, address, RCS number, legal form
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If filing for a Luxembourg permanent establishment, use the PE name and Luxembourg address; do not use full overseas entity details.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Fiscal year and accounting period covered
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the PE's own fiscal year, which must correspond to the home entity's accounting period unless statutory rules require a different cut-off.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit / loss (after commercial adjustments)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only Luxembourg-source business income attributable to the PE; apply arm's-length internal pricing for intercompany flows.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Losses carried forward from previous years (17-year cap)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include any Luxembourg PE losses previously booked and subject to the 17-year carryforward; proof must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation between accounting profit and taxable income (add-backs: non-deductible expenses, tax credits, participation exemption)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Detail cross-border additions (e.g., foreign branch income, corrected double-dip costs) and ensure the net taxable base matches the PE's Luxembourg account.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing fine up to EUR 1,250; late payment interest 0.6% per month; automatic tax assessment; additional administrative fines of EUR 250–2,500 for wilful omission.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% (0% on qualifying dividends under EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive if ≥10% holding is maintained for 12 consecutive months)
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Apply for reduced WHT rate by submitting a valid tax residence certificate (TRC) plus proof of beneficial ownership to the Luxembourg paying agent before payment, and file Form 21 ('Demande de remboursement d'impôt') with the Luxembourg direct tax administration (ACD); the reduced rate is applied at source or reclaimed through a refund procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose withholding tax on royalty and interest payments to non-residents (0% domestic rate). Tax treaty rates for royalty and interest are generally 0% for corporations, subject to beneficial ownership and anti-abuse clauses.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File required if the Luxembourg entity's cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 (aggregate) and the group's consolidated turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Reporting threshold is EUR 750,000,000 consolidated turnover.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg does not apply a British-Offshore-Financial-Centre style ESR regime, but economic substance is required to avoid denial of treaty benefits and participation exemption under the EU ATAD GAAR. Specifically, Luxembourg statutory substance rules for holding, IP, and financing companies require qualified staff, physical offices, and decision-making in Luxembourg. For the IP box regime, the qualifying IP must be developed or improved in Luxembourg.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately under-reporting reverse logistics sales, falsifying returned-item tracking records, or creating fictitious loss carrying certificates to reduce taxable income.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud penalties: fine up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment up to 3 years; civil interest at 0.6% per month; automatic reassessment of the entire tax shortfall.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing the corporate veil permits criminal prosecution of directors; travel bans may be imposed pending trial; civil restitution includes unpaid tax, interest, and a 10% penalty on the under-declared amount.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare or submit Local File/Master File by the statutory deadline, or maintaining materially inaccurate TP records for related-party returns and reverse logistics service fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing reassessment; penalty of 10% of the additional tax due; daily delay interest at 0.6% per month; administrative fine up to EUR 50,000 for non-cooperation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign defective returns may be jointly and severally liable for the tax shortfall if they acted in bad faith; repeated violations can lead to disqualification from board positions.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Absence of real economic activity in Luxembourg: no staff, no physical office, all decisions taken abroad, or the company exists solely to channel payments and exploit treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty benefits and participation exemption; dividend WHT at 25% (rather than 15%) applied; permanent establishment risks; annual fines up to EUR 10,000 for substance legislation non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Civil liability for the entire tax deficiency if the corporate veil is pierced; travel bans imposed by the tax collector; directors may be held criminally for aiding the abuse.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to carry out customer due diligence on merchant refunds, failing to verify beneficial owners of payment chains, or facilitating money laundering through the return-merchandise refund cycle.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines up to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under the Luxembourg AML law of 12 November 2004 (as amended).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are individually subject to criminal sanctions for money laundering offenses; repeated violations may trigger a court-imposed ban from managing any regulated activity in the EU.
